School of Mathematical Sciences, Peking University () is an academic unit of Peking University in Beijing, China. It was established in 1995 through the merger of Peking University's Department of Mathematics and Department of Probability and Statistics. The school offers undergraduate and graduate programmes in mathematics, statistics and related areas, and is associated with research units such as the Peking University Mathematical Institute and the Ministry of Education Key Laboratory of Mathematics and Its Applications.
History
Mathematics teaching at Peking University began with the admission of students to a mathematics programme in 1913, and a Department of Mathematics was created in 1919. In 1952, as part of a nationwide reorganisation of higher education, Peking University's mathematics departments were reorganised into the Department of Mathematics and Mechanics. The mathematics and mechanics programmes were split into separate departments in 1978, and a separate Department of Probability and Statistics was formed in 1985.
The School of Mathematical Sciences was formed in 1995 by merging the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Probability and Statistics. The Beijing International Center for Mathematical Research (BICMR) was founded at Peking University in 2005 and is affiliated with the university's mathematics research and graduate training.
In 2017, Peking University's mathematics and statistics disciplines were included in China's first round of the "Double First-Class" initiative for world-class universities and disciplines.
Academic structure
The school comprises departments of Mathematics, Probability and Statistics, Information and Computational Science, and Financial Mathematics. It offers undergraduate majors including mathematics and applied mathematics, statistics, information and computational science, applied statistics (biostatistics track), and data science and big data technology, as well as doctoral programmes in pure and applied mathematics, computational mathematics, and probability and statistics.
Research
Research at the school covers areas in pure and applied mathematics and statistics, and is supported by institutes and laboratories including the Peking University Mathematical Institute (established in 1980) and the Ministry of Education Key Laboratory of Mathematics and Its Applications (established in 1989). The school is also associated with interdisciplinary research centres such as the Peking University Statistical Science Center and the National Engineering Laboratory for Big Data Analysis and Application Technology.
Notable alumni
* Wang Xuan – computer scientist and inventor; studied in Peking University's Department of Mathematics and Mechanics.
* Zhang Yitang – number theorist; studied in Peking University's Department of Mathematics in the late 1970s and early 1980s.
* Zhiwei Yun – mathematician; entered the School of Mathematical Sciences in 2000 and later received a New Horizons in Mathematics Prize (2018).
* Wei Zhang – mathematician; graduated from the School of Mathematical Sciences in 2004 and later received a New Horizons in Mathematics Prize (2018).
* Ruochuan Liu – mathematician; studied at the School of Mathematical Sciences (1999–2004) and later joined Peking University as faculty.
* Hong Wang – mathematician specializing in harmonic analysis; alumna of Peking University’s mathematics program and recipient of the Salem Prize and the Gold Medal of the International Congress of Chinese Mathematicians (ICCM).
